# Accuracy

Each plug-in is compiled beside upstream's own C++ at the pinned commit and both are fed the same int16 signal at 44.1, 48, 96 and 192 kHz, over seven settings of the parameters: upstream's defaults, all 0, all 1, all 0.25, all 0.75 and two random draws. Upstream's noise and `rand()` get the seeds the port uses, so dithered output compares sample for sample. The figures are the worst distance from upstream's output rounded to int16, in int16 steps, over every sample of every case. The bar is 2: 1 step of error plus the rounding on each side.

`full` is the full-precision variant every desktop runs. `single` is the variant a board without a double FPU runs; where it reads `= full`, the plug-in's single-precision loop strayed outside the bar and boards run the full one ([why](plugins.md#full-precision-on-boards)).

Two faults are planted in each plug-in with parameters, to show the comparison would notice: a gain error of 1 part in 4096, which it must catch, and the first parameter read from the wrong place. A wrong parameter can be one the settings tried barely move, so a miss there is shown, not failed. Cases where upstream's own output goes infinite or NaN have nothing to compare against and are named instead.
